question: Question linked to image nº17 You receive a biopsy of the duodenum of a 38-year-old woman with no other clinical information. What is the most likely diagnosis?

options.opa: Intestinal lymphoma: infiltration of the lamina propria and the superficial epithelium by a monotonous lymphoid cell population.
options.opb: Gluten-sensitive enteropathy (celiac disease): intestinal villi atrophy, increased inflammatory infiltrate and intraepithelial lymphocytosis.
options.opc: Lymphangiectasias: dilatation of lymphatic vessels located in the lamina propria of the mucosa.
options.opd: Whipple's disease: accumulations of macrophages of wide cytoplasm and microvacuolate in the lamina propria of the mucosa.
options.ope: Giardiasis: presence of Giardia lamblia trophozoites on the intestinal surface.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Biopsy of the duodenum -> histological examination -> identification of specific tissue changes -> 70% CHAIN: Infiltration of lamina propria and superficial epithelium by monotonous lymphoid cell population -> characteristic of intestinal lymphoma -> likely diagnosis -> 80% CHAIN: Intestinal villi atrophy, increased inflammatory infiltrate, and intraepithelial lymphocytosis -> features of gluten-sensitive enteropathy (celiac disease) -> possible diagnosis -> 60% CHAIN: Dilatation of lymphatic vessels in lamina propria of mucosa -> characteristic of lymphangiectasias -> potential diagnosis -> 50% CHAIN: Accumulations of macrophages with wide cytoplasm and microvacuolate appearance in lamina propria of mucosa -> indicative of Whipple's disease -> less likely diagnosis -> 40% CHAIN: Presence of Giardia lamblia trophozoites on intestinal surface -> suggestive of Giardiasis -> unlikely diagnosis -> 70%
analysis: Based on the biopsy findings described, the most likely diagnosis is gluten-sensitive enteropathy (celiac disease) characterized by intestinal villi atrophy, increased inflammatory infiltrate, and intraepithelial lymphocytosis.
